title: A Kato energy average extends ordinary positive LSI to complex polar norms

statement.quantifiers: Every legal finite KMS Hermitian-noise generator and arbitrary square complex Q.
statement.assertion: E_H(Q)>= [E_H(|Q|)+E_H(|Q*|)]/2; a supplied positive L2 LSI therefore controls both left/right polar density entropies and gives the stated sine hypercontractive curve.
assumptions: Hermitian noises including exact Lyapunov drift.
Explicit polar-power conventions and supplied ordinary positive L2 LSI; not a complete reference LSI.

inputs: Polar Q=U|Q|, positive LSI and audited KMS sine profile.
outputs: Complex energy/entropy comparison and ordinary weighted norm curve.
interface.precision: Exact finite forms; singular powers by continuity for p>1.
costs: A spectral gap alone does not supply the required LSI.

proof_mechanism: Real HS Cauchy-Schwarz compares the two Hermitian noise products.
Drift matches the average of the absolute-value drift terms exactly.
Apply positive LSI separately to left/right polar densities on the SAME system.
Exact p-derivative of log weighted norm is the AVERAGE relative entropy divided by p^2.
Sine profile with pprime=alpha2 p^2 sin(pi/p)/2 yields the tangent curve.
obstructions: One right density alone gives the wrong complex norm derivative.
Untouched-reference LSI cannot be borrowed from ordinary positive LSI.

potential_uses.transfer_gate: Charge the polar convention and both density entropies instead of inserting a false complete LSI premise.

review.source_reported: Source reports internally reconstructed and adversarially audited mathematics with scoped finite checks; no independent ingestion proof reconstruction, scientific replay, external correctness or priority clearance.
